lessons: Start with immersive hypothetical scenarios ('सोचो, तुम...') to consistently achieve high early retention (>1.0 at 10%).
Avoid immediate exposition heavy drops: lines explaining complex mechanical processes or heavy data early cause the steepest drop-offs (e.g., 22.5% loss at 13%).

Maintain strong comparative performance by avoiding excessive technical jargon or dense anatomical metrics mid-video, as seen in the sharp 50% retention drop for dense T. rex bite-force explanations (down to 0.16).
Keep pacing brisk past the 50% mark; videos that maintain better relative performance at the end (e.g., 0.49 vs_similar_end) avoid slow narrative plateaus.
Not enough data to confirm if countdown elements affect retention negatively, as all analyzed videos have 'countdown': false.
worst_moment_types: Heavy technical explanation and data dumps right after the hook
Complex structural or anatomical breakdowns (e.g., bone-by-bone computer simulation details)
best_hook_types: Imaginative, high-stakes hypothetical scenarios involving the viewer ('सोचो, तुम...')
Challenging common pop-culture assumptions immediately in the opening line
